You read transcripts of Bitcoin videos. For each EXCERPT below, the sentences inside <selected> are a clip
that may be shown on its own. Use the whole excerpt (what comes before and after) to judge the selected words. You do
not know how the clip will be used.

<excerpt label="71a70788e75b17f227d8" channel="Blockware Solutions" video_title="I Studied Every Stock Market Crash of the Last 40 Years (Here’s What Happens Next)" published="2026-11-06T17:52" show_date="2026-11-06">The question is how much of the index are these companies? And that's what this pie chart here shows us. Over half of the index is AI -related companies. And so the AI portion of the NASDAQ and the S &P 500 at that as well, it's too big to fail. These AI stocks, if these AI stocks continue to go down, you will get contagion in the markets. You will get contagion in the economy. If the AI stocks go down, the indexes go down, Spending in the economy goes down, business income goes down, and you get this recession. You get this domino effect. And we've seen in recent history what the government does every time there might be a recession, they fire up the money printers and they lower interest rates. I expect nothing different if we were to get a prolonged drawdown in these AI stocks. Now, one of the narratives behind this week's move in these AI stocks is that because of... the Democrats taking control of the House, the Senate, and many state and local governments that they're going to impose anti -Data Center, anti -AI regulation. Now, that certainly could be on the table. However, the markets are reacting poorly regardless of jurisdiction. So the chart here shows over the past five days how these AI -related stocks have... performed, but broken down by individual states. You can see Democrat -controlled states in blue, Republican -controlled states, Idaho there in red. And then in purple, I think this is the one that's most important. This is Texas. This flipped from Republican to Democrat this week. Yet - The one AI exposed company in the NASDAQ that's in Texas is actually up over the past five days. So if it were this blue to red shift that was really catalyzing this drawdown in the AI stocks, you would expect a company in a state that flipped from red to blue to really be leading that drawdown. And that's just not what we've seen over the past week. And to drive this point home even further. AI is really not a partisan issue. Nearly 50 % of all adults in the US, according to a Gallup survey, quote, strongly oppose a data center in their area. Now, I wonder how many of those survey participants would still strongly oppose a data center if they knew that their entire stock portfolio hinges on continuous buildout in this sector. So what does this all mean for Bitcoin? Well, I think Bitcoin is showing incredible strength and resilience holding the line right here at 76,000. Typically, on these bloodbath type days for tech stocks, Bitcoin gets hurt even worse. But Bitcoin's only down about 5%, which is par for the course for this volatile orange coin. And it's actually down less than the QQQ itself on Thursday. And so Bitcoin is really digging its heels in the dirt right now. <selected>And if it can hold the line here at the short term holder cost basis, I think we're going to see Bitcoin closed 2026 above 90,000, which is about where the year started.</selected> And as we took a look at in the start of the video, here is Bitcoin and the short term holder realized price. So everyone who's bought Bitcoin in the past six months, their cost basis is precisely where Bitcoin is at right now. This is support. During uptrends, newer market participants buy when the price reaches their cost basis. There's this psychological level that, hey, we've pulled back a little bit. This is where my cost basis is. I'm going to buy the dip. This is good value. You see that during up trends. You see the opposite during downtrends. The price has a relief rally. It reaches their cost basis. The new participants in the market, they're like, hey, I'm going to take some chips off the table. I'm going to sell now that we've got a little rally going, and then you start to get a downtrend. On top of the short term level, right now the market structure from an on -chain perspective looks strikingly similar to the recovery period of 2023. So coming out of that last bear market, what you saw on chain was a lot of coins consolidating into wallets that don't sell.</excerpt>

For each excerpt answer:
- "speaker_changes_inside": does the speaker change inside the selected words? "yes" / "no" / "uncertain"
- "view": whose view the selected words express: "own_sincere" (the speaker's own sincere assertion), "attributed"
  (someone else's view, quoted or reported), "hypothetical", "conditional" (true only under a condition), "sarcastic",
  "question", "reading_aloud" (reading a post or article), "ad_read", "joke", or "uncertain"
- "referents": every pronoun or pointing word in the selected words (it, they, this, that, he, she, today, here...)
  that points at something specific, with what it refers to; "inside": true if the selected words themselves give
  its antecedent or the predicate that completes it (an ellipsis completed by an earlier selected sentence: "It's not
  Bitcoin that's getting hacked. It's other intermediaries." = other intermediaries are getting hacked), or it points
  only at a general topic the clip presupposes; "inside": false if a listener needs the words before or after the
  selection; "changes_assertion": "yes" if resolving it differently would change WHAT THE SPEAKER ASSERTS, "no" if
  not, "uncertain". Leave out words that point at nothing outside: a dummy "it" ("it's raining", "it's not X that
  ...", where X is in the selection), and a generic "we" / "you" / "they" meaning people in general
- "conditions": any condition or time frame that governs the selected words, and whether it is INSIDE them
- "retraction": "none", or what the speaker later in the excerpt WITHDRAWS, REVERSES, CORRECTS or MATERIALLY LIMITS
  about the selected words ("actually I misspoke", "that said, I don't believe that", "but that only holds if ...").
  A later elaboration or warning that is CONSISTENT with a condition already stated inside the selected words is not
  a retraction ("none"); it would be one if the selected words had dropped that condition
- "time_ok": "yes" if every time word in the selected words (today, now, this week, just, recently, a "current"
  price) still holds on the show date given when the video was published (both on the excerpt), or there is none;
  "no" if it is stale; "uncertain"
- "proposition": in one sentence, what the speaker asserts in the selected words, read in context
- "certainty": "certain", "likely", "possible", "speculative" or "uncertain"
- "speaker_is": "host" if the excerpt shows that the speaker of the selected words is the channel's own host,
  "guest" if it shows a guest or another person speaking them, "uncertain" otherwise; "speaker_evidence": the exact
  words of the excerpt that show it (copied exactly, e.g. the host's own "welcome back to my channel"), or ""
